sentences.text:
---- Respondent
For Applicant : Shri Ss Baghel, Advocate.
For Respondent/State : Shri Lalit Jangde, Dy. GA  Hon'ble Smt. Rajani Dubey, J  Order On Board 18/01/2023

The applicant has filed this first application under Section 438 of CrPC as she is apprehending her arrest in connection with Crime No.288/2022 registered at Police Station-Ambagarh, Distt.
Rajnandgaon (CG) for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 506, 294 and 34 of IPC.
02.
As per the prosecution case, complainant Karuna Jamulkar was married to co-accused Pushpendra Jamulkar on 6.5.2020.
However, after few days of marriage, her husband and mother-in-law i.e. present applicant started ill-treating her in connection with demand of dowry and even abused her filthily and beat her.
When such torture and harassment became unbearable, she left her matrimonial home and started residing at her parental home since 10th May, 2022.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
The marriage of son of the applicant and the complainant was a love marriage.
The complainant is a quarrelsome lady and used to raise dispute on every trivial household matters.
The applicant never assaulted or ill-treated the complainant for dowry.
The applicant is suffering from heart disease and blood pressure and taking treatment for the same since 2017 at Ramkrishna Care Hospital, Raipur.
The applicant is a reputed person and if arrested, it would cause an irreparable loss to her.
There is no apprehension of her absconding or tampering with the evidence or influencing the witnesses and conclusion of the trial is likely to take some time

;
therefore, the applicant may be released on anticipatory bail.
04. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application.

05. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
06.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the nature of allegations made against the applicant who is 68 years old and suffering from heart disease; there is no apprehension of the applicant absconding or tampering with the evidence or influencing the witnesses and that conclusion of the trial is likely to take some time, without commenting anything on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the application is allowed.
